rationale: The literature in the provided SOURCES directly supports that seizures occur in a minority of individuals with LRRC7-related intellectual developmental disorder 77, specifically reported in 6 of 33 individuals (18.2%) in the primary multi-centric cohort study (Willim et al., 2024) and corroborated by subsequent case reports noting tonic seizures (Khan et al., 2026) and early childhood absence seizures (Popp et al., 2017). OMIM #621415 confirms that seizures are present in only a minority of LRRC7 cases. While the provided excerpts do not explicitly assess SYNGAP1 cohort metrics within the text, the documented penetrance of epilepsy in LRRC7 (~18%) provides strong discriminating evidence confirming that epilepsy is low-penetrance in LRRC7 compared to high-penetrance epileptic encephalopathies.

evidence.text: In a multi-centric cohort of 33 individuals with heterozygous LRRC7 variants, varying types of seizures were reported in 6 individuals (18.2%), confirming that seizures occur in a distinct minority of patients.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic responsiveness and long-term electroclinical trajectory of seizures in LRRC7 patients under specific anti-seizure medications (ASMs)?
new_directions.rationale: While absence and tonic seizures are documented in probands, larger standardized registry studies are needed to determine if refractoriness ever emerges and which specific ASMs yield complete control.

new_directions.question_text: Does seizure susceptibility in LRRC7-related disorder correlate specifically with variant class (truncating loss-of-function vs. missense in the PDZ/LRR domains)?
new_directions.rationale: Functional studies show differing biochemical perturbations between LRR-domain variants (impaired PP1 binding) and PDZ-domain variants (impaired synaptic targeting), which may modulate network excitability differently.
